hints.content: To find the image of $\triangle ABC$ under the dilation, we can dilate all of $\triangle ABC$'s vertices and connect them.

For example, point $\blueD C$ is $10$ units below $P$, so its image is $\goldD{\dfrac12}\cdot10=5$ units below $P$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Triangle A B C. Point B is twelve units to the right of point P and twelve units down, Point C is ten units down from point P, and Point A is eight units right of point P and eight units down. There is a dashed line to highlight vertically the ten units down point P. There is another plotted point that is five units down from point P.

hints.content:
Let's do the same thing with the remaining vertices.

Since our scale factor is $\goldD{\dfrac12}$, every side length in $\triangle A'B'C'$ will be $\dfrac{1}{2}$ the length of the corresponding side in $\triangle ABC$.

Another way to think about it is that since our scale factor is $\goldD{\dfrac12}$, every point in the image will be exactly in the middle between its corresponding point in the pre-image and our center $P$.

Connecting the vertices of the image, we get the following mapping:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Triangle A B C. Point B is twelve units to the right of point P and twelve units down, Point C is ten units down from point P, and Point A is eight units right of point P and eight units down. There is another triangle graphed that is triangle A B C with a scale factor of one half from point P. The new triangle the Point B prime is six units to the right of point P and six units down, Point C prime is five units down from point P, and Point A prime is four units right of point P and four units down. The distance between C prime and B prime is approximately six point one units. The distance between C prime and A prime is four point one units. The distance between A prime and B prime is two point eight units.

question.content:
**Draw the image of $\triangle ABC$ under a dilation whose center is $P$ and scale factor is $\dfrac{1}{2}$.**
